_meta.purpose: BD-curated per-cited-host action playbooks. Each playbook matches one host_type (and optionally host_subtype) and produces a templated action item the merchant can execute. PR-G wires playbook selection into the merchant audit's action_items list.
_meta.owner: BD team for content; engineering reviews schema only.

schema_per_playbook.applies_when: match criteria: host_type required, host_subtype optional
schema_per_playbook.concrete_next_step: 1-sentence 'this week' task — what the merchant should DO first, with specifics (URLs, contact methods, sample sizes). Distinct from body_template (which describes the strategic rationale).
schema_per_playbook.severity: critical | high | medium | low — applied uniformly across all instances of this playbook

_meta.matching_priority: When multiple playbooks could match a host, the more specific match wins (subtype > type). Unknown hosts (type='unclassified') match the catch-all generic_unclassified playbook.
_meta.schema_v2_changes: Added concrete_next_step field to every playbook (PR after merchant feedback that actions read as 'sample format' instead of deep-dive specifics).

editorial_pitch_review_site.concrete_next_step: This week: send a 100-word pitch email to {host}'s product/tip line referencing their existing category roundup, attach 3 product samples + a 1-page brand differentiation note (what makes you different from the brands they already cover).

editorial_pitch_fashion.concrete_next_step: This week: identify the {host} editor covering your category (LinkedIn / masthead) and send a trend-led pitch (not a product-led pitch — fashion editors want a STORY angle), with 3 sample looks + a 100-word seasonal trend hook.

editorial_pitch_beauty.concrete_next_step: This week: send PR samples + INCI list + claims/clinical data to {host}'s beauty editor; beauty editorial requires substantiation, not just samples — include the specific testing or formulation differentiator that makes you newsworthy.

wholesale_department_store.body_template: {coverage_note} {competitors_phrase}{outreach_hint} Wholesale onboarding is a multi-quarter process; expected timeline: {timeline_low}-{timeline_high} weeks for vendor approval.
wholesale_department_store.concrete_next_step: This quarter: submit through {host}'s vendor portal. Department-store wholesale needs a line sheet (10-30 SKUs minimum), wholesale price list at 50% of retail, EDI compliance documentation, and proof of $500k+ annual brand revenue. Start the application even if you're not ready — the review is multi-step.

wholesale_luxury.body_template: {coverage_note} {competitors_phrase}{outreach_hint} Luxury wholesale requires established brand authority + price point fit; expected timeline: {timeline_low}-{timeline_high} weeks.
wholesale_luxury.concrete_next_step: Likely premature for early-stage D2C — luxury wholesale wants $1M+ brand revenue, established editorial coverage in Vogue / Harper's Bazaar / Elle, and a complete look-book. Build editorial visibility first; circle back to {host} after 2-3 luxury-tier press hits.

wholesale_beauty_retailer.body_template: {coverage_note} {competitors_phrase}{outreach_hint} Beauty specialty retailers run accelerator programs (Sephora Accelerate, Ulta Sparked) for D2C/indie brands as a faster track than direct wholesale.
wholesale_beauty_retailer.concrete_next_step: This month: apply to {host}'s D2C/indie accelerator (Sephora Accelerate or Ulta Sparked) — these are the front-door for D2C beauty brands and run application cycles 1-2x/year. Have ready: brand deck, $500k+ revenue evidence, hero SKU clinical data.

wholesale_fashion_marketplace.body_template: {coverage_note} {competitors_phrase}{outreach_hint} Fashion marketplace onboarding is faster than department-store wholesale; expected timeline: {timeline_low}-{timeline_high} weeks.
wholesale_fashion_marketplace.concrete_next_step: This month: apply via {host}'s vendor application page with a complete line sheet, wholesale price list, and 6-month sell-through projections. Fashion marketplaces respond faster than department stores but want strong sell-through evidence.

wholesale_wellness_retailer.concrete_next_step: This month: apply via {host}'s wholesale form with full ingredient/sourcing documentation + GMP/FDA certifications + COA per batch. Wellness retailers gate on substantiation more than scale.

wholesale_mass_market_retailer.body_template: {coverage_note} {outreach_hint} Note: mass-market retailers typically prefer brands at scale; if you're early-stage D2C, prioritize specialty retailers + editorial first.
wholesale_mass_market_retailer.concrete_next_step: Likely premature — mass-market wholesale wants $5M+ brand revenue and established distribution. Skip {host} for now; revisit once you have specialty-retailer wholesale + editorial coverage from the higher-priority actions.

wholesale_regional_retailer.concrete_next_step: Confirm market relevance first: does {host}'s region match your shipping / market priorities? If yes, apply via their vendor portal. If no, skip.

marketplace_listing_mass_market.body_template: {coverage_note} {outreach_hint} Marketplace listings (1P + 3P) get D2C brands AI-channel grounded faster than editorial because product feeds index directly. Expected timeline: {timeline_low}-{timeline_high} weeks.
marketplace_listing_mass_market.concrete_next_step: This week: enroll in {host}'s 3P seller program (faster than 1P vendor onboarding) — list your hero SKU with rich content (A+ content / brand store), then enable Amazon Brand Registry. Listings index in grounded retrieval within 2-4 weeks.

marketplace_listing_fashion.concrete_next_step: This week: apply via {host}'s seller / vendor onboarding form with line sheet + wholesale terms. Fashion marketplaces are faster to list than they are to actually merchandise; budget for paid-feature ads to lift visibility.

creator_partnership_video.body_template: {coverage_note} {outreach_hint} For sleepwear/fashion/beauty: focus on mid-tier reviewers (10k-100k subs) who already cover your category. Sponsored reviews land in grounded retrieval within {timeline_low}-{timeline_high} weeks of upload.
creator_partnership_video.concrete_next_step: This month: identify 3-5 mid-tier creators (10k-100k subs) on {host} who already publish category roundups including competitor brands. Send a sponsorship pitch — typical rate is $50-500/video at this tier — with a custom discount code so you can track conversions.

creator_partnership_social.body_template: {coverage_note} {outreach_hint} Social-first creators drive social pickup but lower AI-channel grounding weight than YouTube long-form.
creator_partnership_social.concrete_next_step: Lower priority for AI-channel attribution. Spend first on YouTube long-form creators (higher grounded-retrieval pickup). Use {host} for category awareness + paid ads, not for editorial-style endorsement.

generic_editorial.concrete_next_step: This week: identify the right editor at {host} (LinkedIn / masthead) and send a 100-word product pitch + sample. Editorial pitches need a story angle, not just product specs.

generic_retailer.concrete_next_step: This month: apply via {host}'s vendor portal with line sheet + wholesale price list + brand deck.

generic_marketplace.concrete_next_step: This week: enroll in {host}'s seller program with hero SKU listing + rich product content.

generic_unclassified.body_template: This host appeared in your audit's grounded sources but isn't in our registry yet. Worth a quick research pass — visit the site, identify whether it's editorial / retailer / marketplace / brand competitor, and assess whether it's a relevant outreach target for your category.
generic_unclassified.concrete_next_step: This week: visit {host}, identify what they cover, decide whether they're editorial / retailer / brand competitor / noise. If they're a relevant editorial or retailer, file a follow-up to add them to our registry.
